title: The four jars

data.source: The 1200 stored runs of Phoenix development harness P18-LOOP1-2026-10-08 (a synthetic world in which the scored population games a published classifier), rescored here.
data.licence: none needed (synthetic, generated by the study from seeds)

prediction: As Phoenix records: keeping track of which inputs are the agent's own echo adds nothing over a generic drift detector in clean worlds, raises false alarms when a harmless outside change lies along its own outputs, and gains a small edge only in confounded worlds, where a plain randomised intervention does as well.
baseline: A generic input-drift detector, black-box shift detection on the model's own score, the same statistic with the provenance labels removed, and randomised intervention on the published output.
why: Every stored figure was recomputed exactly. The provenance statistic is shift detection along the agent's published outputs: no better than a generic detector in clean worlds, fooled by a harmless shift half the time, and matched by ordinary randomised intervention where it does help. Phoenix grades it NOTHING, with one small effect PENDING.
phoenix_status: "Development only: synthetic worlds, no preregistration, no ledger rows." Grades: DESIGN for the harness and controls; NOTHING for detection beyond black-box shift detection in clean worlds; PENDING for the confounded-world edge. "This note does not declare FLAME." The principle itself is "a testable engineering hypothesis".
